title: Preserve exact Gaussian sums with reversible rounding and complete ports
body:
The actual C0/C2 ports now have a nearest-grid Gaussian backend that preserves each pair's **exact sum**, commutes with global Gaussian unit phases, and has an exact same-grid inverse without rounding history. Both stored dirty banks return exactly under the complete two- or three-call inverse program. The previous sufficient accuracy and signed-width bounds remain valid. This is a numerical implementation contract, not a new kappa or native supplier admission.

For s=x+y and d=x-y, choose a minimum-norm Gaussian center c(s) with component-sum parity equal to that of s, then set d'=i*(d-c)+c. Equal-parity sums use c=0; mixed-parity sums use a unit selected by the sign of the odd component. The inverse uses -i and the same conserved sum. The [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a4173e810c4d34a1d13b9745af123ad0ec6cfed5/research/conservative-gaussian-rounding/PROOF.md) classifies **all minimum-error centers in this affine-on-difference family**. Every input also attains the least Euclidean error among all grid-valued outputs: zero or exactly one squared pair-error unit. Reversibility alone is credited prior work, not the claimed improvement.

For N=8^f, the complete native call preserves **4^f independent spectator-fiber sums**. These give exact error constraints, including after the corresponding monomial change of observable. The new kernel is installed through an explicit backend argument in the retained complete port; no source patch or hidden inverse oracle is used.

The limitations are constructive too. Rounded axes do not commute on a concrete four-coordinate input. Pair exchange, common translation and additivity fail. The proof shows two incompatibilities within the stated affine family. An inverse must reverse the literal stage order; the result does not make arbitrary native graph cycles consistent or justify applying ideal linear identities to nonlinear rounded maps.

Both CPython3.12.13 registered modes pass13,122 pair cases,52,488 phase cases,49 center calibrations,36 completed calls,1,008 exact fiber observables,24 complete port directions with dirty return, and12 aligned predecessor ports. A separate Gaussian-rational tensor convolution and three-bit monomial interpreter check actual inputs at every paid cut. The primary24 port executions charge16,720 butterflies,167,200 data additions,33,440 exact half shifts and267,520 range checks. Nonzero rounding, nearest-even information loss, wrong inverse order, aliasing, overflow, invalid domains and all four retained source corruptions are checked. [Receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a4173e810c4d34a1d13b9745af123ad0ec6cfed5/research/conservative-gaussian-rounding/RESULT.json).

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/conservative-gaussian-rounding
```

The complete direct bill includes every native pair, source mixing, four or six monomial passes, route setup, checks, reads, writes and owned cleanup. It is O(fN) bounded-word work or O(fN*(w+f)) indexed bit work, with O(N*(w+f)) stored bits. The proof gives an eight-word pair schedule and retains the actual port width. It does not provide an accelerated recursive tariff or a fixed multitape schedule. Physical routing, recursive funding, stock, complete caller/outer admission and all five selected assumptions remain open.

All17 committed package/input files pass byte/mode and official-export checks. Read-only Git-free, empty-PATH normal/optimized replays agree and leave all18 exported files unchanged. Hosted replay and planning both passed at the published head: [run41560838174](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41560838174). The initial registered run caught a tuple/list serialization mismatch in the receipt comparison; the producer now emits JSON arrays explicitly, and both full modes pass without changing the mathematical receipt. Full-history preflight is unavailable in this shallow checkout; all runtime predecessors are byte-exact package inputs. No network or side-branch object is needed for replay. Independent human and proof-kernel acceptance are unclaimed.

Only `research/conservative-gaussian-rounding/` is added. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5475#discussioncomment-19363827). Canonical main7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a, priority8/selected6030, remained unchanged at submission. Live Discussions, open PRs and main source searches were checked; earlier reversible lifting, the rounded-loop obstruction, PR6480 zero-padding and PR6499/6506 selected scalar records are distinct and credited where relevant. Sparse history, arbitrary diffs and unpublished work remain overlap limits.

Prepared for Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no subagents. [NOTICE](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a4173e810c4d34a1d13b9745af123ad0ec6cfed5/research/conservative-gaussian-rounding/NOTICE) credits JoyboyBrian/PR5485 and the PR4743 port/error sources, Tekalign's reversible lifting, Arham Tahir's numerical/collision work, Nick Petalas's error context, JoyboyBrian's native-loop result, Cinna Davis's frame-additivity result, and all retained P104/native/compiler lineage. Lattice parity and integer lifting are established mathematics. No merge, closure or frontier change is requested.
